name: United States
summary_text: The United States demands real caution from trans visitors — and uniquely among Western nations, is the subject of official trans-traveler warnings from at least eight European allied governments (Germany, Finland, Denmark, and others, March 2025) following executive orders requiring federal documents to reflect sex assigned at birth. A German traveler, Jessica Brösche, was detained at the US border for weeks and deported (January 2025); a CBP officer faces a lawsuit for alleged sexual contact with a trans traveler at Boston Logan Airport. Trans Americans have been stranded with mismatched passports. Enforcement extends into daily life: in April 2025 a trans woman was arrested and jailed overnight under Florida's bathroom law — believed to be the first such arrest — and a trans man was detained by police in South Carolina for using a women's restroom. State-level bathroom laws, misgendering statutes, and a hostile federal posture coexist with strong protections in blue states and cities.

sources.title: Know Your Rights: Airport Security | A4TE
sources.claim_summary: Advocates for Trans Equality 'Know Your Rights' guide to US airport security (TSA): body-scanner flags, pat-downs, documentation mismatches, and how to request alternative screening.

sources.title: US State Revokes Gender-Affirming Identification | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Mar 2026): 'US State Revokes Gender-Affirming Identification' — across Kansas, trans people receive letters voiding their driver's licenses under a law invalidating birth certificates and IDs that do not match sex assigned at birth and barring bathroom use inconsistent with it.

AP (Feb 2026): 'New law puts Kansas at vanguard of denying trans identities on drivers licenses, birth certificates' — Kansas prevents transgender people from changing markers on birth certificates and licenses; rights groups call it a template for other states.

sources.title: Bans on Transgender People Using Public Bathrooms and Facilities According to their Gender Identity - Movement Advancement Project
sources.claim_summary: Movement Advancement Project equality map: bans on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity - 9 states + 1 territory ban such use in all government-owned buildings and spaces including K-12 schools, colleges and more; some bans extend to airports, public parks and other government spaces.

sources.title: Trans, nonbinary travelers left stranded as passport rules change
sources.claim_summary: USA Today (March 2025): how the new State Department rule blocks trans travellers - Trump's executive order requires all government identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth; passports are issued only with markers matching 'biological sex'; first-person account of a trans man flagged at airport security and accused of using a fake ID due to a licence/passport mismatch.

AP (Apr 2025): 'Transgender student's arrest for violating Florida bathroom law is thought to be a first' — a trans student declared 'I am here to break the law' and was handcuffed in a women's restroom at the state capitol; civil-rights attorneys say it is the first known arrest under the state's bathroom-restriction law.

sources.title: Passport + Identity Document Information for the Transgender Community - Lambda Legal
sources.claim_summary: Lambda Legal FAQ on passport and identity-document information for the transgender community (updated March 2026): what the January 2025 'Gender Order' means for passports, REAL IDs and other documents; the restrictive passport policy is in effect (as of Nov 2025); practical guidance for travellers, noting it is informational, not legal advice.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026
sources.claim_summary: Erin In The Morning anti-trans national legal risk assessment map (July 2026): Idaho becomes the fourth 'Do Not Travel' state for transgender people - bathroom usage can lead to 5-year prison sentences; South Carolina expanded its bathroom ban to universities; state-by-state risk grading for trans people.

sources.title: HRC | Travel & Passport Rights for Transgender People
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Campaign resource on travel and passport rights for transgender people: what the January 2025 executive order ('sex at conception' on all government ID) did - the State Department immediately stopped allowing trans, nonbinary and intersex people to update sex designations.

sources.title: Countries issue advisories about trans people traveling to the United States | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Apr 2025): 'Countries issue advisories about trans people traveling to the United States' — multiple foreign governments warn their trans citizens about travelling to the US over identity-document and data rules.

Axios (March 2025): Trump's transgender rights rollbacks prompt allies to adjust travel warnings - at least eight European countries (including Finland and Denmark) adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the US; advisories follow detentions of European citizens over visa issues.

sources.title: The new transgender rights battles beyond sports and gender medicine | Vox
sources.claim_summary: Vox (March 2026): the fight over transgender rights in America has entered a new phase - the policy fight is moving well beyond sports and youth medicine into broader areas.

sources.title: Identity Document Laws and Policies - Movement Advancement Project
sources.claim_summary: Movement Advancement Project equality map on identity-document laws and policies: state-by-state driver's license gender-marker change processes and options (22 states + D.C. allow M, F or X); accurate markers reduce risk of violence and discrimination.

sources.title: Is the United States safe for LGBTQ+ travellers in 2026? | Queer Compass
sources.claim_summary: Queer Compass travel-safety guide (April 2026): is the US safe for LGBTQ+ travellers in 2026? - same-sex activity legal, but protections vary heavily by state; trans, non-binary and intersex travellers face extra uncertainty around passports, visas, gender markers, facilities and healthcare; border/visa processes can involve social-media and device checks; credible reporting of travellers cancelling trips or facing extra scrutiny.

Condé Nast Traveler (Feb 2025): what to know about the new policy on passport gender markers - the State Department stopped processing X-marker passports and markers not matching sex assigned at birth; existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; new applications processed only as M or F per supporting documents.
